intervals.label: Expression of Interest
intervals.note: Year precision only (Evian workshop, 1992); the exact date within 1992 is not stated in the excerpt consulted.
intervals.quote: an expression of interest for a dedicated general-purpose heavy-ion detector was presented at Evian in 1992

intervals.label: Letter of Intent
intervals.note: INSPIRE experiment record 1110642 gives the same date in date_proposed (1993-03-01). End = the approval date recorded in the same INSPIRE record (date_approved).
intervals.quote: On 1 March 1993, ALICE collaboration submitted a letter of intent to the CERN LHC Committee, proposing the construction of a heavy-ion experiment dedicated to the study of the physics of strongly interacting matter produced in nucleus-nucleus collisions.

intervals.label: Technical Proposal and addenda
intervals.note: Year precision only: the detector paper confirms the sequence (Expression of Interest -> Letter of Intent -> Technical Proposal -> Addenda -> 1997 approval) but does not give the Technical Proposal's exact date in the text consulted. CERN Courier ('New kid on the block') dates the forward-muon-spectrometer addendum to 1995 ('included as an addendum to the Letter of Intent in 1995'); the Technical Proposal itself was not consulted, so this interval is marked approximate rather than verified.
intervals.quote: The ALICE concept evolved via the Expression of Interest [2] and a Letter of Intent [3] towards the Technical Proposal [4] and its Addenda [5–7]. The experiment was approved in 1997

intervals.label: approval
intervals.note: INSPIRE's experiment record gives date_approved = 1997-02-06. CERN Courier's account (an extract dated April 1997) reports the same approval in less precise terms ('has received the green light'); the ~2-month gap between the INSPIRE date and the Courier's April 1997 publication date is most likely just publication lag and is not treated as a conflict.
intervals.quote: ALICE has received the green light to proceed towards final design and construction.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: Some subdetectors (PHOS, TRD, PMD, EMCal) were only partially installed by the paper's mid-2008 press date and were completed for the high-luminosity ion runs from 2010; this partial-completion detail is not separately modelled as its own interval.
intervals.quote: Most detector systems will be installed and ready for data taking by mid 2008 when the LHC is scheduled to start operation, with the exception of parts of PHOS (1 out of 5 modules installed), TRD (4 out of 18), PMD, and EMCal (construction started in 2008).

intervals.label: commissioning and first collisions
intervals.note: date_started in the INSPIRE experiment record (2009-11-23) matches the well-documented date of the LHC's first collisions, which every LHC detector recorded the same day.

end.note: Run 1 ended in early 2013 with Long Shutdown 1; no ALICE-specific or CERN page consulted gives the exact end date.

intervals.label: Run 1
intervals.note: This is an LHC machine-wide schedule fact (all four main LHC experiments, including ALICE, took data through the same run); no ALICE-specific start/end announcement was found beyond the general LHC schedule pages.
intervals.quote: The first attempt for collisions at 7 TeV (3.5 TeV per beam) is scheduled for 30 March.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 1
intervals.note: Bounded by the sourced facts that Run 1 ended in early 2013 and the LHC's second run covered 2015-2018 (machine-wide fact, not ALICE-specific).

intervals.label: Run 2
intervals.note: Machine-wide LHC fact applied to ALICE, which recorded pp, p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions throughout Run 2.
intervals.quote: On 3 December, the LHC's second run came to an end after three fantastic years.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 2 / ALICE 2 upgrade
intervals.note: ALICE's own upgrade (new ITS2 pixel tracker, GEM-based continuous-readout TPC) was completed in 2021, ahead of the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 2 beam restart in July 2022; both dates are recorded (see Run 3 interval for the beam-restart date).
intervals.quote: In 2021, the collaboration completed a major upgrade, denoted ALICE 2, to enhance its detector capabilities and continue its scientific journey at the LHC in Runs 3 and 4.

intervals.label: Run 3
intervals.note: Machine-wide LHC fact applied to ALICE, now running with the upgraded ITS2/TPC (ALICE 2).
intervals.quote: A round of applause broke out in the CERN Control Centre on 5 July at 4.47 p.m. CEST when the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) detectors started recording high-energy collisions.

end.note: CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 / ITS3 and FoCal upgrade
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: ALICE's own detector is being upgraded in this shutdown: the ITS3 (replacing the three innermost tracking layers) and the FoCal forward calorimeter. CERN news of 25 April 2024, written by the ALICE collaboration, says the two upgrades 'have recently been approved for installation during the next long shutdown of the LHC'. The ALICE Collaboration's January 2026 paper (arXiv:2601.07405) says 'During the LHC Long Shutdown 3 (2026-29) ALICE will replace its three innermost tracking layers by a new detector'. ALICE's site says 'Further detector upgrades are being carried out for Run 4 until the end of 2033'; that describes the upgrade programme for Run 4 and does not date the end of this shutdown. The 2024 and 2026 ALICE-related sources give LS3 as 2026-28 and 2026-29; this interval follows CERN's later schedule, in which the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030. The 2024 article dated the ITS3 and FoCal installation to early 2028; no 2026 source consulted confirms the current installation schedule. ALICE takes no data in this period because the LHC is off. Start and end are the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 dates. CERN's 5 August 2026 item says 'The cryogenics team has been running the warm-up sequence since LS3 began on 29 June 2026' and that the stored helium is kept 'ready to be used again once the accelerator resumes operation in mid-2030'; CERN's 29 June 2026 article says 'The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030'. The end is a schedule value, not a reported event.
intervals.quote: Two detector upgrades of ALICE ... have recently been approved for installation during the next long shutdown of the LHC

physics_goals.quote: quark-gluon plasma, a state of matter thought to have formed just after the Big Bang
physics_goals.value: Study the quark-gluon plasma, a state of matter thought to have formed just after the Big Bang

physics_goals.quote: Elliptic flow is sensitive to plasma properties like shear viscosity and equation of state.
physics_goals.value: Measure collective (elliptic) flow to determine the shear viscosity and equation of state of the quark-gluon plasma

physics_goals.quote: Quarkonia production probes deconfinement and parton recombination whereas resonance parameters (masses, branching ratios) is sensitive to chiral symmetry restoration.
physics_goals.value: Use quarkonium production to probe deconfinement and parton recombination in the plasma phase

physics_goals.quote: Heavy flavour production, and jet fragmentation will probe parton kinematics and energy loss in the plasma phase.
physics_goals.value: Study heavy-flavour production and jet fragmentation to probe parton energy loss in the quark-gluon plasma

summary.plain: ALICE is CERN's dedicated heavy-ion experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. By colliding lead nuclei instead of protons, it recreates the quark-gluon plasma, an extremely hot and dense state of matter thought to have filled the universe microseconds after the Big Bang, and studies how ordinary matter freezes out of it.
summary.technical: General-purpose heavy-ion experiment at CERN LHC Point 2, optimised for the physics of strongly interacting matter and the quark-gluon plasma in Pb-Pb, p-Pb and pp collisions. Central barrel (ITS, TPC, TRD, TOF, HMPID, PHOS, EMCal) inside the L3 solenoid (0.5 T, reused from LEP) plus a forward muon spectrometer; approved 1997, first LHC collisions recorded November 2009, ALICE 2 upgrade (new ITS2 pixel tracker, GEM-based continuous-readout TPC) completed 2021 for LHC Run 3.

unique_capabilities.quote: ALICE employs essentially all known PID techniques: specific ionization energy loss dE/dx, time-of-flight, transition and Cherenkov radiation, electromagnetic calorimetry, muon filters, and topological decay reconstruction.
unique_capabilities.value: Comprehensive particle identification across a wide momentum range, combining specific-ionisation dE/dx, time-of-flight, transition and Cherenkov radiation, electromagnetic calorimetry, muon filters and topological decay reconstruction

unique_capabilities.quote: The central part covers polar angles from 45◦ to 135◦ and is embedded in a large solenoid magnet reused from the L3 experiment at LEP.
unique_capabilities.value: Reuses the L3 experiment's LEP-era solenoid magnet as its central magnet
